hero.title: Long conversations about AI
hero.lede: I no longer make videos, but I still accept a few long-form invitations. These are the ones worth your hours, newest first. They are in Brazilian Portuguese; YouTube's auto-translated captions do a decent job.

items.7uFqDMwQ4_8: A segment on SBT News's News Manhã. The UN General Assembly took up the risks of AI this week, and I talked about the warnings from the AI companies themselves, the risks to global security, and AI and deepfakes in the Brazilian elections.
items.U3bZavG8qQY: Lessons from 37 days of full immersion in vibe coding: 653 commits, about 144,000 lines and 8 projects in production. What agents can and cannot do, which business models make sense, and why the one-shot prompt is a myth.
items.4c7pbOxYn_A: Almost five hours on how AI changed in a year: the tipping point, what the owners of the biggest models do not say, why dumb questions burn more tokens, jobs, and which AI is best for programmers.
items.9aWa-eCmWYE: The end of the hype era. Why excitement about AI is inversely proportional to knowing how it works, and how I used frontier models to multiply my output on seven real projects without replacing the engineer.
items._Hl9wiLkns4: With writer Ricardo Cavallini and astrophysicist Roberta Duarte: will superintelligence arrive, what a GPT really does, and a long detour through quantum physics and quantum computers.
items.sf4Gxf0LiKo: My first long conversation about AI on Flow: what it really does today, its limits, its history back to the 1960s, and what nobody tells you about quantum computers.
